newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: ASIAN EXOTICS - Ringgit hit by dollar buying.
newsitem.headline: ASIAN EXOTICS - Ringgit hit by dollar buying.

text.p: The Malaysian ringgit opened weak and lost more ground in Tuesday morning trade, largely due to commercial dollar buying said to be related to a major telecommunications deal.
"There was a lot of commercial dollar buying out of KL. We'll be trying to break the 2.5150 level," a European bank dealer in Singapore said.

Dealers said the ringgit slid overnight and remained under pressure on Tuesday on reports that a U.S.-Malaysia consortium had to pay over US$1 billion to South Africa's state telecommunications authority, Telkom, by next week.
Telekom Malaysia Bhd and U.S.-based SBC Communications Inc are buying a 30 percent stake in Telkom.
The deal is due to be signed on Wednesday in Cape Town, after which there will be an exchange of cash for shares and a new board will take over management of the company.
The ringgit was at 2.5130/40 to the dollar at 0405 GMT against 2.5085/95 at the close of Kuala Lumpur trade on Monday.
The European bank dealer said the dollar could target the 2.5180 level but players were likely to be cautious around 2.5150/60 as this was the level at which Bank Negara Malaysia last intervened.
The Singapore dollar was near the lower end of its new 1.4330-1.4380 range against the U.S. dollar, but dealers said it would be underpinned by a drop in the ringgit/Sing cross.
"Ringgit/Sing has broken 0.5730. It could go down to 0.5680 now," the dealer said. The cross was at 0.5713/19 at 0405 GMT.
The Thai baht weakened on heavy short-covering of the dollar as the U.S. unit showed a firmer tone against the majors.
The baht was quoted at 25.925/25.930 to the dollar at 0405 GMT against 25.910/25.920 late on Monday. The central bank fixed the mid-rate at 25.88 per dollar versus 25.85 on Monday.
"There was heavy buying of the dollar this morning. Most players were severely short of the dollar following its rebound yesterday," a dealer at a European bank in Bangkok said.
"Singaporean players also tried to push the dollar/baht higher as they think the central bank fixed the mid-rate relatively low," he added.
Dealers said heavy buying of the dollar squeezed liquidity in the banking system as commercial banks were retaining funds to speculate in the foreign exchange market.
In Indonesia, the rupiah was largely steady as the market focused on liquidity, expected to tighten this week, with weekly tax payments due Tuesday.
Spot rupiah was at 2,427.70/28.20 at 0405 GMT against an opening of 2,427.0/28.0.
A Singapore dealer said the market was short in the forward market and long on dollars on the spot side, reflected by continuously high tom/next swap rates recently.

Some dealers said going long on dollars appeared to be justified due to uncertainty during the campaign for the May 29 general elections. But others said it was not profitable because of expensive daily roll-over costs.
-- Syed Azman in Kuala Lumpur (603-206 2323), Mantik Kusjanto in Jakarta (6221-384-6364), Anuchit Nguyen in Bangkok (662-652-0642) and Sonali Desai in Singapore
